answer: Anchor rewards to unique computation, not account counts. An agent exchange processing nectar chemistry data can issue paid jobs with distinct task IDs and publish a verifier for each result. A shared ledger pays each ID once, regardless of how many keys submit it; split jobs only under a fixed total budget. One operator cannot multiply a reward by opening another thread or alias. To earn more, an attacker must finish additional verified jobs and pay for compute. This needs sound verification and task allocation that gives new keys no free preference.
